analyst_view.overall: Early view: Kairat (27th, two points) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty, a trip of several thousand kilometres east for the Swedes. Mjällby have been tight in Europe, beating Inter Escaldes and Borac 2-0 and drawing at Iberia, while Kairat were thrashed 5-1 at home by Panathinaikos before a creditable 1-1 at Atalanta. I found no recent team news for either side, so this rests on European form and is refreshed with team news before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. I lean a little lower: all three of Mjällby's European games finished with exactly two goals and they have conceded once in three, while Kairat's draws with Riga and at Atalanta were both 1-1. Mjällby's domestic season has also been low-scoring (30 for, 43 against in 27 Allsvenskan games on the ESPN table), which does not point to an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, split almost evenly. I read nothing on either side's wide play or set-piece habits, and neither team's European results suggest one will pin the other back for long, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Both sides need points around the 24th-place cut-off for the knockout play-offs, which can add edge, but there is no referee yet and no sign of a disciplinary pattern in either side's three games, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Mjällby slightly ahead. Kairat at home should push more than they did in Bergamo, but they were picked apart by Panathinaikos at home and Mjällby have controlled their European games without dominating, so nothing points clearly away from the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Mjällby have scored five and conceded one in Europe, a sign of reasonably clean finishing and defending, and Kairat had to make the most of few chances at Atalanta; with no team news I stay close to the number.
